messages.subject: Prediction grid densities
parts:
Hello list,

 

I have a specific question about the densities appended to the prediction grid (under the Data tab) in Distance after running the DSM prediction. I have a very hard time matching it to the density plot shown in the Analysis results. My densities in the grid seem to be a factor 10^9 higher and not consistently indicating where the decimal position is. This gives me problems when exporting the data to an external GIS platform as some values show as being a factor 10 lower than they are supposed to be. As it is not consistent I cannot correct it by a formula. I have dug around for a few days in the R code etc. and cannot figure out why the numbers is or where in the code they are appended. The rest of the analysis run as expected and all relevant units are in meters. Do anyone have a suggestion on how to solve the problem?

 

I know I should probably migrate the projects to R but my R skills are sadly lacking at the moment.

 

Best Regards

messages.author: 7482eee8d2863d12
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Prediction grid densities
parts:
Hi Rasmus,

I wonder if this might be a problem with regional differences in decimal
notation (dots vs commas etc)? This should not be a problem in Distance
for Windows but has been on occasion, historically. You could try
setting your region to UK and see if that fixes it.

Another option, if you're doing some more "advanced" work with the dsm
engine, would be to switch to working entirely in R. This gives
considerably more flexibility with your analysis and output options.
Running analyses in debug mode allows to access the R input files as one
way of learning the ropes -- there are also the workshop materials from
Dave Miller's last DSM workshop freely available at
http://workshops.distancesampling.org/online-dsm-2020/
(although likely not as good as getting it directly from Dave :) ).

As a halfway house, you can run analyses in R using the debug mode
outputs to see what's being generated by R. For example, I opened the
"Dolphins" example from the Sample Projects that come with R, and ran
the analyses in there up to analysis number 6, which does the
predictions. I then ran that one in debug mode, and found the file it
creates "in.r" in a temporary directory. The line that generate the
prediction grid is

dsm.predict.6<- predict(dsm.5,newdata=grid.6, off.set=grid.6$area)

and then the one that writes this to file is (in my case - your
directory will differ)

sink(file='C:\\Users\\len\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\dst43677\\res.r',append=T)

so I could have a look at that file and see what's in it. I could also
just have a look at dsm.predict.6 in R.

I hope this is helpful - just ping on me off the list if you want to
discuss more and we can report back to the list once resolved.

Cheers, Len

messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Prediction grid densities
parts:
Rasmus

I'm not positive I understand your question, but see if this clears up you challenge.

Looking at the prediction grid values in the Data tab (last column, shown with red arrow), those values are densities (with the dolphins example that ships with Distance for Windows) per square meter.   The values are in scientific notation 4.87 x 10^(-10) for the first prediction grid cell.  The values get to be as large as 10^(-7) near the centre of the study area.

Against what are you comparing those numbers in the Analysis result; are you referring to the legend in the response surface plot?


At least for this dolphins project, the values from the data table are consistent with the legend in the figure.  Most of the study area is in the darkest shade, indicating values < 10^(-7).  Am I misunderstanding?
